name: Square Attachments Leave Nonpeelable Strong Carriers Unchanged
statement: Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, and let $K$ be its canonical graph three-core. For every nonempty coordinate set $D$, the reduction $H^D$ is nonpeelable exactly when $K^D$ is, and then the two embedded reductions are equal. No acquired pair of any square attachment meets a coordinate $e$ with nonpeelable $H^{\{e\}}$. At such an $e$, relative peelability of either section to the common negative overlap is also identical for $H$ and $K$. Consequently, if the crossing graph of $K$ is not two-connected, reduction descent from $H$ has length at most one and the same unique cut-vertex terminal obstruction, even when $H$ itself has no separator.
proof: Reconstruct $H$ from $K$ by ample one-concept additions with acquired coordinate pairs $I$. Under reduction by $D$, one such step either disappears or remains a one-corner addition with acquired support $I\setminus D$. If the earlier reduction is nonpeelable, full-coordinate strong descent says it already shatters every surviving singleton; hence $D\subseteq I$ is impossible and the two reductions are equal. For $D=\{e\}$ this also proves $e\notin I$. The new concept then changes only one $e$-section, by a rank-two addition disjoint from $e$; rank-two relative-extension invariance preserves peelability to the fixed overlap in both directions. Iterating proves all assertions, and applying separator strong descent to $K$ gives the final conclusion.
